module_description: Module 29 is the integrative capstone: teams of 4-5 solve a real listening/analysis problem end-to-end - collect, clean, model, visualize, interpret, present - using an Indonesian public dataset. Deliverables: pipeline code, documented dataset, dashboard, insight presentation, and a short report with limitations and ethics note. Assessment uses a rubric covering data, method, insight, ethics and communication; sample scenarios include election discourse analysis, brand sentiment on TikTok, hoax/detection studies, and coordination analysis.
core_concepts: From descriptive numbers to defensible insights
Presentation of analytics to non-technical clients
learning_outcomes: C6 Design and execute an end-to-end social media analytics project
C5 Evaluate and critique an analytics study (own and peer)
C4 Present insights and limitations to a non-technical audience
methods_models: Full pipeline: API/scrape collection, cleaning, topic/sentiment/network/engagement models, dashboard, report
evaluation_metrics: Rubric-based: data quality, method validity, insight quality, ethics, communication (each 0-4), plus reproducibility check of a clean run
pitfalls_limitations: Scope creep, non-reproducible pipelines, over-claiming insights, unmanaged personal data, unequal team contribution
tools_stack: Everything from the course stack; team Git repository and issue tracking; optional containers for reproducibility
commercial_platforms: Capstone sponsors may be local NGOs, media or SMEs; commercial tools used only if a partner provides access
tools_access_cost: Keep total spend near zero by using open protocols and public datasets; document any licensed access
lab_activities: Weekly milestones (W1 problem, W2 data, W3-4 analysis, W5 dashboard, W6 report and presentation) with peer review
datasets_apis: Indonesian public datasets: election discourse on X/Bluesky, TikTok brand comments, hoax corpora, creator metrics
assessment_methods: Ethics/DPIA note graded with a rubric; includes defence of sampling, retention, anonymisation and disclosure choices
data_collection_workflow: Identify data and legal basis -> DPIA/risk assessment -> collect only what is needed -> anonymise -> document retention and disclosure -> preserve the ethics note
textbooks: Course texts as reference; capstone reading packs per scenario
key_papers: 2024-2026 method papers cited in each module as the method baseline
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: capstones increasingly involve video/short-video data, LLM-validated annotation, and agentic pipelines - reflecting current analyst practice
industry_relevance: Capstone output mirrors what industry panels expect in entry-level screening: an end-to-end pipeline, a documented dataset, an interactive dashboard, and a 10-minute insight presentation; sponsors can be local NGOs, media, or SMEs.
localization_context: Default capstone datasets are Indonesian (X/Bluesky politics discussions, TikTok brand sentiment, hoax-news corpora, local election discourse), with options for cross-lingual replication using English datasets.
ethics_regulation: Every capstone must submit an ethics/DPIA note: which platform, which data, what was collected, retention plan, anonymization, and what conclusions are and are not supportable.
case_study_scenarios: Team project on a real Indonesian issue or brand question with a sponsoring organization (or a clearly scoped public dataset).
deliverable_format: Dashboard + reproducible repo + final report + 10-minute presentation
